title: The Sigil of Ironhollow Again
premise: Edmund Kavanagh, a bone-carver who hears the dead, discovers his own name and tonight's date in a century-old book of prophecies kept by the Guild of Impossible Things. The prophecy foretells that a soul sold to the court beneath Ironhollow will be devoured at moonset unless someone steals it back — and the soul belongs to Wren, the orphan girl the guild raised as its own. Edmund descends into the mountain with a disgraced guild archivist and a ghost who remembers being royal, trading pieces of his own memory as currency for passage through the court's bone gates. In the end he wins Wren's soul back but loses every recollection of her, so it is Wren who must teach him their found family all over again — proof that love outlasts the self that made it.
about_author: Marguerite Hartwell is a former cathedral archivist who spent a decade cataloguing funeral records before turning to fiction, a habit that still haunts her prose. She writes in a converted bell tower in the north of England, where she keeps an extensive collection of carved animal bones and refuses, politely, to explain why.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Tonight
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. While balancing the guild's impossible accounts, Edmund hears a dead clerk whisper about a page no one has read in a hundred years. He finds tonight's date and his own name inked in the prophecy ledger. Emotional beat: quiet dread — the comfortable order of his life cracks open on an ordinary evening.

chapters.title: What the Guild Sold
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He confronts Guildmistress Ashka, who admits the guild brokered Wren's soul to the court beneath Ironhollow decades before she was born — a debt inherited like property. Emotional beat: betrayal; Edmund realizes the family that sheltered him also trafficked in its children.

chapters.title: A Ghost Who Was Royal
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Seeking a guide, Edmund wakes the ghost sealed in a whalebone door: Seraphine, a forgotten queen who remembers the court below and hates it. She agrees to lead him for a price to be named later. Emotional beat: wary alliance; two lonely beings strike a bargain neither trusts.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Confession
chapters.summary: Tobias Vane's POV. Tobias, the archivist who falsified the sale records out of cowardice, begs to come along to atone. He reveals the prophecy can be rewritten if the original contract is destroyed at its signing place. Emotional beat: guilt seeking redemption; the party becomes three.

chapters.title: Down the Bone Gates
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The three descend through gates of fused skeletons that demand payment in memories. Edmund pays first with his mother's face, then his wedding day that never was. Emotional beat: sacrifice begins; power is shown as something that eats what you love.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Seraphine's POV. Reunited with the court that exiled her soul from its throne, Seraphine navigates its glittering cruelty while Edmund poses as a debt-collector. They learn Wren's soul is caged as a lamp for the Bone King's table. Emotional beat: seduction and horror; corruption wears beautiful faces.

chapters.title: The Price Named
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Seraphine names her price: Edmund's memories of Wren, every one, so she can feel again what family meant. He agrees without telling the others. Emotional beat: heartbreak chosen freely; love measured against the self.

chapters.title: Moonset Rising
chapters.summary: Tobias's POV. The theft of Wren's soul-lamp goes wrong; Tobias burns the original contract mid-escape, unmaking the court's claim but collapsing the tunnels. The Bone King hunts them through the dark. Emotional beat: desperate momentum; courage discovered in the least likely member.

chapters.title: The Devouring Hour
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. At moonset, Edmund offers his remaining memories wholesale to buy Wren's release, and Seraphine turns on the court, reclaiming her name to shatter the Bone King's crown. Wren's soul flies free as Edmund forgets her entirely. Emotional beat: climax — ruin and triumph indivisible.

chapters.title: Carving New Bones
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Above ground, Wren grieves that Edmund survived but doesn't know her — then begins teaching him their family, story by story, carving new memories like bone-work. Seraphine departs into dawn, finally free. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; found family rebuilt from nothing, stronger than memory.
